parsed.notes: No treatment/currency findings raised under Lens A. No text/*.txt files were disclosed, so quote-fidelity review is limited to lake pinpoints.

reasons: Lake identity is Schmerber v. California, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1966, with official citation 384 U.S. 757.
Lake pin-770 is star-verified and says there was no time to seek out a magistrate and secure a warrant, supporting the dissipation/time-lost holding.
Lake identity is Missouri v. McNeely, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 2013, and citations.all includes 569 U.S. 141.
Lake pinpoint frames the issue as whether natural metabolization categorically creates exigency in every drunk-driving case and states the rule as no, supporting the no per-se holding.
residual_risks: citations.display is null in the lake record, but the cited reporter appears in citations.all and the lake pinpoint header.

reasons: Lake identity is Kentucky v. King, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 2011, with official citation 563 U.S. 452.
Lake pin-op8 describes the officers' own knock-and-announce prompting occupants to destroy evidence and says the rule turns on whether police acted lawfully before the exigency arose.
residual_risks: The table row paraphrases rather than quotes the exact Fourth Amendment formulation.

defect.evidence_quote: Evidence obtained under a genuinely independent warrant is not tainted by a prior illegal entry.
defect.problem: The case and citation exist, but the row states Segura as an affirmative secure-premises-to-prevent-destruction rule. The disclosed lake rule is independent source/taint, not a holding that officers may secure premises from within because evidence may be destroyed or removed.
defect.proposed_fix: Tighten the row to say Segura involved officers securing an apartment until a warrant arrived and held later warranted evidence was not tainted by the prior entry, or add a verified opinion text/pinpoint for the secure-premises proposition.

reasons: Lake identity and citation match Segura v. United States, 468 U.S. 796 (1984).
The only disclosed Segura rule is independent-source/taint; it does not verify the row's broader destruction-preservation holding.
residual_risks: A full opinion text might support a narrower securing-premises proposition, but it is not disclosed here.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use Segura for independent-source/taint unless a verified securing-premises pinpoint is added.

reasons: Lake identity is Illinois v. McArthur, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 2001, with official citation 531 U.S. 326.
Lake pin-334 is star-verified and supports a temporary seizure backed by probable cause to prevent loss of evidence while police diligently obtain a warrant.
Lake identity is Cupp v. Murphy, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1973, with official citation 412 U.S. 291.
Lake pin-296a is star-verified and supports probable cause, very limited intrusion, and ready destructibility; pin-296b disclaims a full Chimel search without arrest/warrant.
Lake identity is Mincey v. Arizona, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1978, with official citation 437 U.S. 385.
Lake pin-392 states there is no murder-scene exception and seriousness alone does not create exigency; pin-393 limits seizure to plain-view evidence during legitimate emergency activities.
Lake input_case_name is Birchfield v. North Dakota, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 2016, with official citation 579 U.S. 438.
Lake treatment scope says breath tests are valid as search incident to arrest and blood tests are not, supporting the cross-doctrine relevance stated in the row.
residual_risks: The disclosed lake scope does not address consent as a separate possible justification.

defect.problem: The case, citation, year, and plurality label are verified, but the disclosed Mitchell record only supports a general plurality yes; it does not verify the stronger 'may almost always' formulation or the defendant-rebuttal parenthetical.
defect.proposed_fix: Tighten to 'generally yes (plurality)' or add verified opinion text/pinpoint for the 'almost always' and rebuttal language.

reasons: Lake identity is Mitchell v. Wisconsin, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 2019, with official citation 588 U.S. 840.
Lake treatment scope confirms a plurality opinion, but the disclosed pin does not contain the row's more specific rule language.
residual_risks: Full opinion text might verify the exact formulation, but it is not disclosed.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use 'generally yes (plurality)' unless a verified pinpoint is supplied.

defect.evidence_quote: doctrine when it is the officers' own knock-and-announce that prompts the occupants to begin destroying evidence. ## Rule The test keys on whether the police acted lawfully before the exigency arose:
defect.problem: The black-letter rule contains a verbatim King quote and pinpoint to page 462 that cannot be verified from the disclosed evidence. The King lake record has only a slip-summary pinpoint with quote_fidelity mismatch and no disclosed text file; the black-letter approval threshold is also not verifiable from the provided records.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace the verbatim King quote with a paraphrase supported by lake pin-op8, or add a verified opinion text/star-page pinpoint for page 462. Split the rule into separately supported propositions and supply the required affirmative approvals for black-letter status.

reasons: No text/Kentucky v. King opinion is disclosed, and the lake King pinpoint does not contain the quoted phrase 'by engaging or threatening to engage in conduct that violates the Fourth Amendment.'
The disclosed McArthur pin supports a temporary seizure/freeze while obtaining a warrant, but it does not verify the whole black-letter 'enter and act' formulation at that breadth.
No disclosed field shows the required >=2 affirmative approvals for the black-letter rule.
residual_risks: The propositions may be correct in the full opinions, but they are not fully verifiable from the disclosed evidence.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use only verified paraphrases unless the exact King quote and pinpoint are added.
